prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

BAGHDAD, Iraq (CNN)  -- Coalition forces found 26 bodies buried in mass graves and a bloodstained "torture complex," with chains hanging from walls and ceilings and a bed connected to an electrical system, the military said Wednesday. Twenty-six bodies were found in mass graves near a "torture complex" discovered by coalition forces. The troops made the discovery while conducting an operation north of Muqdadiya, Iraq. From December 8 to 11, the troops who found the complex also killed 24 people they said were terrorists and detained 37 suspects, according to a statement issued by Multinational Division North at Camp Speicher in Tikrit. The moves were part of an operation called Iron Reaper that has been in progress across northern Iraq for the past few weeks. The complex was in an area thought to be an al Qaeda in Iraq haven and operating base, the military said. Iraqis had told the military about the site during an earlier operation. "Evidence of murder, torture and intimidation against local villagers was found throughout the area," the military statement said. Ground forces first found what appeared to be a detention facility, which was one of three connected to the torture complex, Multinational Division North said. One of the facilities appeared to have been a headquarters building and a torture facility, it added. As the area was cleared, the bodies were found. Eventually, 26 bodies were uncovered in mass graves next to what were thought to be execution sites, the military said. The bodies are believed to have been dead between six and eight months, according to a gruesome military video shot at the scene. Some had their hands tied behind their backs. Identification is proving to be a challenge because of advanced decomposition. Photos given to the news media show a filthy bed wired to an electrical system, with an outlet hanging from wires on the wall. In the video, troops point out rubber hoses and boxing gloves, a ski mask and a blood-covered sword and knives. Other still photos show an entrance to the underground bunker and barbed wire stretched outside it. A short distance away from the complex, troops found a bullet-riddled Iraqi police vehicle. Some of the bodies may belong to Iraqi police, according to the military video. The operation netted nine weapons caches, which have been destroyed, the military said. They included anti-aircraft weapons, sniper rifles, more than 65 machine guns and pistols, 50 grenades and a surface-to-air missile launcher and platform, the statement said. Also found were mines, pipe bombs, rocket-propelled grenades, mortar tubes and rounds and 130 pounds of homemade explosives. E-mail to a friend .

The operation, aimed at rooting out insurgent strongholds in the volatile region, led troops to a site that revealed the brutal methods employed against the local population.

Inside the complex, soldiers found chilling evidence of systematic violence. The facility contained chains used to restrain prisoners, an electrified bed apparently designed to inflict pain through electric shocks, and an assortment of other implements of torture. Even more disturbing was the discovery of mass graves located near the complex. As troops searched the surrounding area, they exhumed 26 decomposed bodies from the burial sites. Some of the victims had their hands tied behind their backs, indicating they had been bound and likely executed. Forensic assessments suggested that many of the bodies had been in the ground for as long as six to eight months, pointing to a prolonged campaign of killing.

The findings painted a stark picture of the terror inflicted upon villagers in the region. Coalition officials characterized the site as evidence of the murder, torture, and intimidation that al Qaeda-linked militants had used to control and coerce the local community. The discovery underscored the human cost of insurgent activity in the area and reinforced the objectives behind Operation Iron Reaper, which sought to dismantle such networks and restore security to communities that had long lived under the threat of violence.

The operation, conducted jointly with Iraqi security forces, targeted a compound that intelligence had linked to insurgent activity. What troops found inside, officials said, went beyond weapons caches or planning materials.

"Upon entering the structure, forces discovered several individuals who showed visible signs of prolonged mistreatment," the military statement read. "Medical personnel provided immediate care to those found on site. The evidence recovered will support ongoing efforts to hold accountable those responsible for these acts."

## Evidence Recovered at the Scene

According to the statement, troops recovered restraints, improvised implements, and documentation from the location. Officials also reported finding recorded material—video and photographs—that appeared to have been produced by those operating the site.

The recovered footage, which officials said would be reviewed as part of the investigation, reportedly depicted individuals in confinement. The military did not release the material publicly, citing the ongoing investigation and the dignity of the victims.

"The conditions documented here are consistent with a pattern we have seen from these networks," a coalition spokesperson said in the statement. "These groups target the very population they claim to represent."

## Those Found on Site

Several detainees were transferred to medical facilities for treatment and evaluation. Their identities and conditions were not disclosed. Officials indicated that some may have been held for extended periods, though they cautioned that the full circumstances remained under investigation.

The military said Iraqi authorities would lead follow-up efforts to identify the victims, notify families, and pursue those who operated the facility.

Sites of this nature have surfaced periodically throughout the conflict, as insurgent networks established informal detention and interrogation locations in areas under their influence. Human rights organizations have long documented abuses committed by armed groups operating outside any legal framework.

"Each site uncovered adds to the record," the coalition statement noted. "Our commitment is to support Iraqi partners in restoring security and ensuring that those who commit these crimes face justice."

# U.S. Forces Uncover Mass Graves, Torture Complex in al Qaeda Stronghold North of Muqdadiya

**BAGHDAD, Iraq** -- U.S. and Iraqi forces have discovered mass graves and an underground torture bunker during operations against an al Qaeda in Iraq stronghold north of Muqdadiya, the U.S. military announced, describing conditions that offered a grim window into insurgent brutality in the volatile Diyala province.

Troops swept through the area in recent days as part of ongoing operations to clear al Qaeda-linked militants from the region, roughly 60 miles northeast of Baghdad. The offensive uncovered evidence of what commanders characterized as a systematic campaign of intimidation, torture and execution aimed at controlling the local population.

## Grim Discoveries

Soldiers uncovered multiple burial sites containing the remains of individuals believed to have been killed by the insurgents, according to a military statement. Forensic teams were working to identify the bodies and determine the circumstances of the deaths.

Nearby, forces discovered an underground bunker described by officials as a torture chamber. Inside, troops reportedly found chains, restraints, and instruments consistent with the abuse and interrogation of prisoners. Military officials said the complex appeared to have served as a detention and killing site for those who resisted al Qaeda's rule.

"What we found here demonstrates the brutal nature of this enemy and their complete disregard for human life," a military spokesman said, noting that such facilities were used to terrorize residents into compliance.

## Suspects Detained, Weapons Seized

During the operations, coalition forces detained several suspected insurgents believed to be connected to the site. Officials did not release the exact number of those captured but said interrogations were ongoing as part of efforts to dismantle the local al Qaeda network.

Troops also uncovered significant weapons stockpiles in the area, including caches of munitions, roadside bomb-making materials, and other ordnance. Explosives ordnance disposal teams destroyed the weapons to prevent them from being used against coalition and Iraqi forces or civilians.

The discoveries came amid a broader push in Diyala province, which had become a refuge for insurgents fleeing security crackdowns in Baghdad and Anbar province. The rugged, agricultural region north of Muqdadiya had long been considered a haven for militant activity.

## Ongoing Operations

Military officials said clearing operations in the area were continuing as forces worked to establish security and root out remaining insurgent elements. The efforts were part of the larger troop increase aimed at stabilizing regions where al Qaeda in Iraq maintained a foothold.

Local residents, many of whom had fled the violence, were expected to provide additional information about the site and those responsible for the killings. Iraqi security forces were working alongside U.S. troops to secure the area and support returning civilians.

The military said it would continue to investigate the sites and pursue those responsible for the atrocities.

*CNN's Baghdad bureau contributed to this report.*
